facts.statement: Aardonyx is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur named from Afrikaans for "earth" and Greek for "nail or claw".
facts.quote: Aardonyx (Afrikaans aard, "earth" + Greek , "nail, claw") is a genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaur.

facts.statement: The species Aardonyx celestae was named in honor of Celeste Yates, who prepared most of the initial fossil material.
facts.quote: A. celestae was named after Celeste Yates, who prepared much of the first known fossil material of the species.

facts.statement: The genus was discovered by Australian paleontologist Adam Yates and his team, with findings published online in November 2009 and in print in March 2010.
facts.quote: Australian paleontologist Adam Yates and his team's discovery of the genus was published online before print in Proceedings of the Royal Society B in November 2009, and was scheduled to appear in the March 2010 issue.

facts.statement: Aardonyx celestae is known from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation in South Africa.
facts.quote: It is known from the type species Aardonyx celestae found from the Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa.

facts.statement: Aardonyx lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is known from the remains of two immature individuals.
facts.quote: The genus is known from disarticulated bones belonging to two immature individuals.

facts.statement: Both fossil individuals are estimated to have been under 10 years old when they died.
facts.quote: Both individuals are thought to have been less than 10 years old at the time of their death because of the lack of peripheral rest lines in the cortices of sampled bones.

facts.statement: Aardonyx was primarily bipedal but capable of moving on all fours like Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Based on the structure of the hind limbs and pelvic girdle of Aardonyx, the dinosaur normally moved bipedally but could drop to quadrupedal movement similar to Iguanodon.

facts.statement: Aardonyx had a slower gait compared to more basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Features of the femur suggests that the gait of Aardonyx was slower than that of more basal sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Aardonyx was a powerful but slow walker due to a distal fourth trochanter that increased muscle leverage but reduced retraction speed.
facts.quote: The repositioning of the fourth trochanter to a more distal position causes the M. caudofemoralis longus muscle, the main femoral retractor muscle, to have greater leverage (more mechanical advantage) but conversely a decrease in the velocity of femoral retraction; consequently, Aardonyx was a powerful but slower walker than typical prosauropods.

facts.statement: Aardonyx exhibited entaxony, indicating reduced running ability and a wide gait that preceded the full quadrupedalism of later sauropods.
facts.quote: The development of entaxony in Aardonyx provides further evidence for its reduced cursorial ability and wider gauge-gait, which is thought to have preceded obligatory quadrupedalism in sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Aardonyx grew rapidly with growth patterns that were seasonally interrupted.
facts.quote: The osteohistology of Aardonyx shows that it grew rapidly, but that its bodily growth was seasonally interrupted.

facts.statement: Aardonyx displayed a transition toward the bulk-browsing feeding style characteristic of sauropods.
facts.quote: Aardonyx shows a transition toward the bulk-browsing form of feeding characteristic of sauropods.

facts.statement: Aardonyx lacked fleshy cheeks, an adaptation for a wider mouth opening to facilitate bulk browsing.
facts.quote: The absence of a lateral ridge at the caudal end of the dentary is indicative of a loss of fleshy cheeks. This is seen as an adaptation for a wider gape to facilitate bulk browsing and is observed in nearly all sauropods.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the wide, cheekless gape evolved independently in Aardonyx and in later sauropods, as suggested by the more derived state of Chinshakiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Because Chinshakiangosaurus is a more derived sauropodomorph, this suggests that a wide, cheekless gape may have evolved twice in Sauropodomorpha: once with Aardonyx and again with sauropods more advanced than Chinshakiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Aardonyx is classified as the sister taxon to a clade containing Melanorosaurus and sauropods.
facts.quote: Aardonyx is thought to be the sister taxon of a sauropodomorph clade containing Melanorosaurus and sauropods, which are all obligatory quadrupeds, based on a phylogenetic analysis conducted along with the first description of the genus.

rejected.statement: Aardonyx possessed derived skeletal traits including deep hyposphenes and an adult femur length exceeding 600 mm.
rejected.quote: These include derived traits seen in the vertebrae (such as hyposphenes that are as deep as the neural canal and mid-cervical neural spines that are less than twice as long as high) as well as the appendicular skeleton (such as the position of the fourth trochanter over the midlength of the femur and an adult femur length exceeding 600 mm).
